3. Get the content folder onto your laptop
4. Extract the bundle and install the curated skills

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body unchanged since the 2026-08-30 pinned instance (only the maintainer block moved, outside body scope); re-walked every pronoun/demonstrative/definite-noun across all 9 chunks independently and reached the same read. Closest-to-violating: chunk 1 line 22 'The curated security skills install when you extract the bundle.' -- 'the bundle' has no antecedent in lines 1-21 (grepped); the tarball is first named at chunk 4 line 45 (`ae101-content.tar.gz`) and 'the bundle' as a term first appears in chunk 5's own header (line 51), three slides later. Stays inside: this is the file's own established anticipatory-preview device, already used twice in the same chunk-0/chunk-1 span before the reader meets 'the bundle' -- line 7 'the repo picked', 'the curated skills installed', and line 22's own 'the repo itself (picked next)' immediately before it -- so a reader primed by two prior instances of the pattern is not confused by a third, and the sentence's teaching point (skills install automatically at extraction) does not hinge on resolving what 'the bundle' names yet. No other candidate: chunk 3 line 40 'the repo you just picked' resolves to chunk 2 (sequential); chunk 6 line 66 'the candidate-bug screen' resolves to chunk 6 line 62 'the bug screen' (in-chunk); chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked' resolves to chunk 6's bug-screen (same-file backward, rule 1's own domain).

Two off-file links in the body, both named not located: chunk 2 line 34 '[build one from zero](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/build-a-project-from-zero.md)' names the destination in the link text itself; chunk 7 line 76 'Simon Willison, [Vibe engineering](...)' names author and title in the same sentence. Neither points at another file by position ('the opening lecture said'). No cross-file positional callback found anywhere in the body.

Ran this session: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --report --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` -> thinnest chunk is '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' at 17 words, but it carries two self-standing instructions (fetch the tarball via the prompt; manual-download fallback link), not a bare wait-state or context-dependent bullet. No orphan found across the 9 chunks.

Checked all 8 headers against their own chunk content. Closest-to-violating: chunk 4 '3. Get the content folder onto your laptop' (line 43) -- its content (line 45) only asks the student to fetch `ae101-content.tar.gz`, which becomes a folder only after chunk 5's extraction step. Stays inside: nothing in the chunk contradicts the header -- 'folder' names the well-understood eventual outcome of a download+extract pair, and chunk 5's own header 'Extract the bundle' makes the split explicit; no false claim, only an anticipatory label. Every other header matches its content exactly.

Checked all 5 sub-items across all 9 chunks. Ran this session: `grep -n -E "Not [A-Z][a-z]+\. Not " curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` -> 0 hits (no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction). No anaphora/epistrophe triple anywhere. No self-grading superlative. No number-plus-own-retraction -- the in-body '30 to 120 minutes' (line 18) is a plain estimate range, not a number followed by its own retraction, and the runtime-minutes breakdown sits in the maintainer block, out of body scope. No abstraction-noun stack (vocabulary throughout is concrete: repo, tarball, skills, bug, PR). No empty-leg verb triplet -- 'test, branch, commit, and open a PR' (line 60) is four distinct concrete actions, none vacuous. Clean across the file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `grep -n -iE "compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|firing|Connections" curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` -> the only hits (lines 86, 96) sit below the maintainer cut (line 84), out of body scope; zero in-body hits. Ran `grep -n -i surface` -> two body hits, line 17 'user-facing surface' and line 29 'surface area for rules and memory to land on' -- both ordinary engineering usage (the attack-surface/API-surface family), not the repo's writing-surface-as-noun jargon, which the rule itself carves out. 'Plan mode' (line 16) is a real Claude Code product feature, not curriculum dialect. 'Session' (line 38) is the architecture-mandated widget label (`widgets.md`), not narrative dialect. The expanded prompt-block text (chunks 4-6, checked via `node scripts/expand-md.js`) uses plain engineering vocabulary throughout -- no dialect terms found there either.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `grep -n '\*\*' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` over the raw body. Chunk 1 lines 15-18 carry one short (<=4-word) bold handle per bullet ('Trivial bug', 'A small multi-file task', 'A small feature', 'A bigger piece') labelling task-size checklist entries a reader scans to find their own size -- 'checklist item names' is one of the rule's own named handle types, and the reading-list/menu waiver applies by function (a slide meant to be scanned for the reader's entry point, not read straight through); each bold is well under the <=5-word handle cap, so even at 4-per-slide none crosses into a whole bolded sentence (the actual violation shape the rule names). Chunk 3 line 38 '**Session**' is the architecture-mandated widget label, not narrative bold. Chunks 4-6's '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' labels are build-time chrome synthesised from the `{{prompt:<key>}}` marker by `scripts/expand-md.js` -- confirmed against the raw body (lines 47, 55, 64, 68 are bare markers, no literal `**` in source) -- so they carry no authored bold to budget against. Chunk 7 line 76 carries exactly one bolded element, '**Read:**' (1 word), title left plain -- the literal reading-list shape the compendium names as correct. No chunk exceeds its budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content -- verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `grep -n "prework" scripts/build-workbook.js` -> line 377 'All modules: prework first (if present), then ordered modules, then optional.' pushes `t.prework` into the same `allModules` array every ordered module goes through, which line 394 wraps as `<section class="module" id="${m.slug}">` -- the exact wrapper `buildDeckModel` (site/layouts/slides.js) walks to reach the composed deck. Cross-checked against `scripts/slides.test.js` line 41, which fixtures `<section class="module" id="prework">` explicitly as a renderer-guarded case. This resolves the 2026-07-09 failure mode the rule warns about (prework silently dropped from the deck) as fixed and guarded, not merely asserted. All 8 `##` chunks reach the composed deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering -- position is computed, content ordinals are linted.

(exit 0). The hand-numbered '1.'...'5.' step headers (chunks 2-6) are consecutive from 1 with no gaps or duplicates. Ran `grep -n -i step` over the body -- the only in-body hit (line 60) is plain-English 'Now the interactive step', not a numbered cross-reference, so there is no in-file 'Step N' pointer to validate.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` -> 'OK -- 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' (exit 0), and `--report` on the same file returned no matches to clear. The rule's own canonical pre-fix failure ('the repo itself (picked in Step 1 below)') is gone from the current body: chunk 1 line 22 now reads 'Plus the repo itself (picked next)...' -- a reading-order pointer, not a page-position one.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size -- 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran this session: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --report --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/prework.md` -> largest slide 'Bring real work' 196 words / 4 bullets, next '1. Pick THE repo' 142 words / 3 bullets, all remaining chunks well under; summary 'files: 1   slides: 8   oversized: 0 ... (Symbol) every slide is within limits' (exit 0). Chunk 1's runtime fork (`<!--flag:module:earn-the-trust-->` around lines 16-17) resolves through the checker's own fork handling as one branch, per the rule's own note. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All 8 body headings are imperative ('Bring real work', 'Bring to Module 1') or numbered phase/step labels ('1. Pick THE repo' ... '5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') -- the exercise-heading convention, matching what this file is: a task walkthrough, not a lecture. No slide here is a law/consolidation moment where the header IS the teaching, so the claim requirement never triggers. 'Pre-read before Module 1' and 'Bring to Module 1' read as the explicit NOT-violation carve-out (orientation/catalogue-style labels), not mislabelled claims.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked all three classes against every bullet/sentence in all 9 chunks. (a) doctrine restatement -- none found; prework has no prior lens/split/law to re-announce (it is pure M0 logistics), and the 4 task-size bullets (chunk 1) and 3 repo-criteria bullets (chunk 2) each add a distinct move/object, not a recap. (b) self-referential design commentary -- no sentence anywhere tells the student they are inside a pedagogy or names the curriculum's own design intent. (c) aphorism kicker -- closest candidate chunk 6 line 70 'Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there.' (italic closer); stays inside because it is concrete to the specific AskUserQuestion tip just given (lines 66-68) and ties together both the push-back move and the fallback trick just described, not a restatement of the header ('5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness') or a `**The point:**`-style line -- and `grep -rn "small steer\|small trick" curriculum/` confirms this phrasing is not a coined term restated from elsewhere in the corpus (only self-hits). No bullet meeting the 'carries nothing' bar found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is M0 — no prior module's exercise/lecture beat exists for this file to reference, and none is referenced. The only backward-pointing 'the X you did' phrasing is chunk 8 line 80 'The bug you picked', which resolves to this same file's own chunk 6 (same-file sequential, rule 1's domain), not a cross-beat module reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body (grepped for 'guess'/'predict'/'take a guess' — zero hits); prework has no live-demo beat to break.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Review-only surface, never a gate, per the rule's own text. Inventoried the file's two off-file links: chunk 2's structural include-link to the fallback-repo supplementary (named 'build one from zero' in the link text, not located by page position) and chunk 7's external Willison link (named by title/author in the same sentence). Both already satisfy the surviving 'name it, don't locate it' requirement; no in-page fragment links into this file's own deck to check against the settled anchor-routing mechanism.
